prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
This manifesto sets out policies across education, the economy, environment, health, crime, housing, governance, welfare, foreign affairs and taxation.

Education and skills
- Invest £2bn per year funded by a 1p rise in the basic income tax rate.
- Universal high‑quality early education for all 3–4 year‑olds; cap primary classes at 30 within five years; double spending on books/equipment in year one; £500m over five years for repairs.
- General Teaching Council; literacy drive; a streamlined Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; Personal Records of Achievement; stronger discipline and anti‑truancy measures.
- Bring all state schools into one local framework; phase out Assisted Places while encouraging partnership with independent schools; support faith schools subject to standards.
- Individual Learning Accounts; income‑linked student loan repayments; oppose top‑up fees; credit‑based post‑14 system; connect schools to the internet.
- 2% remissible training levy on company payrolls (small firms exempt); aim for 16–19s to receive two days/week education or training.

Economy, enterprise, consumers
- Independent central bank; fiscal “golden rule”; distinguish capital/current spending; promote public‑private partnerships.
- Shift taxation from labour/consumption to pollution; boost saving; benefit‑to‑work incentives; job creation via infrastructure, SMEs and energy efficiency.
- SME support (late‑payment interest, reduced red tape, better finance); regional development agencies; more civil R&D and tech transfer; tourism strategy.
- Stronger competition law; single utilities regulator with consumer focus; tighter financial regulation and redress; clear GM food labelling.

Environment, energy, transport
- Integrate environmental goals across policy; cut CO2 by 30% from 1990 within 15 years.
- Gradual carbon tax offset by cuts to VAT/employers’ NICs; national home‑insulation programme starting with 2m lowest‑income households; higher efficiency standards; promote renewables; no subsidies for nuclear and no replacements at end of life.
- Rail: double passengers and treble freight by 2010; stronger regulation with potential reacquisition of a controlling interest in Railtrack for persistent failure.
- Enable urban road pricing to fund clean, rapid public transport; London Underground to remain public; reduce annual car tax to £10 for ≤1600cc, offset by gradual fuel duty rises; planning to reduce travel.
- Water: leakage targets, fairer charging, share excess profits; stronger countryside protection; animal welfare measures including bans on cosmetic/weapon/tobacco testing.

Health and care
- At least £540m extra annually; restore free eye and dental checks; £200m a year for front‑line staff; maximum six‑month wait from diagnosis to treatment within three years.
- Six‑month halt to finance‑driven closures pending independent audit; end two‑tier GP funding; National Inspectorate for Health & Social Care; national pay body; stronger patient rights; ensure NHS dentistry access.
- Community care: new Carer’s Benefit; national standards, inspection and fair charging; raise care means‑test thresholds as resources allow.

Crime, housing, communities
- 3,000 more police on the beat; youth prevention and restorative justice; CPS overhaul; local crime‑reduction partnerships; Royal Commission on drugs; stronger victim support.
- Build more homes via partnerships; release council capital receipts; new Mortgage Benefit for first‑time buyers (retain MIR for existing borrowers); end rough sleeping by 2000; tackle empty and substandard homes; urban/rural regeneration and transport measures.

Governance and constitutional reform
- Bill of Rights (ECHR in UK law), Human Rights Commission, Ministry for Justice; Freedom of Information; curb quangos; referendums on constitutional issues.
- Proportional representation for all elections; fixed four‑year terms; reduce MPs by about 200; predominantly elected second chamber; party finance transparency.
- Devolution to Scotland and Wales (tax‑varying powers) and English regions where demanded; stronger local government; long‑term move to Local Income Tax and reformed business rates.
- Northern Ireland: power‑sharing, rights protections, policing and justice reforms, cross‑border economic cooperation.

Work, welfare, equality
- Benefit Transfer Programme for long‑term unemployed; raise income tax thresholds by £200 (removing ~500,000 from tax); new 50% rate over £100,000; replace Income Support/Family Credit with a Low Income Benefit; national childcare strategy; voluntary Citizens Service; regionally variable minimum wage; tackle fraud/evasion.
- Pensions: earnings‑linked top‑up for the poorest; flexible retirement 60–70; replace SERPS with funded pensions (accrued rights preserved); portability/security of rights.
- Measures for youth services and families (parental leave/benefit), women (equal pay, part‑time rights), disabled people (civil rights, access), ethnic minorities (anti‑discrimination, fair asylum), and LGBT equality (equal age of consent, repeal discriminatory laws).

Foreign, defence, development, trade
- EU reform and accountability; conditional entry to a single currency via criteria and referendum; CAP and fisheries reform; cross‑border policing cooperation.
- Maintain overall defence level; retain Trident with reduced warheads; support NATO enlargement; non‑proliferation/CTBT.
- UN reform with stronger peacekeeping; support International Criminal Court.
- Aid towards 0.7% GNP within 10 years; debt relief; untied, rights‑linked aid.
- Restrict arms sales to abusers; UN arms register; ban landmines.
- Freer trade with labour and environmental standards; global competition policy.

Tax and transparency
- Annual Tax Contract; tackle waste; fairness and anti‑avoidance.
- Key changes: +1p basic rate for education; +£200 personal allowance; 50% rate over £100,000; +5p per 20‑pack of cigarettes to fund free checks; majority pay lower or unchanged tax; average taxpayer under £100,000 pays about 45p/week extra.
